role: computational image screening, not human acceptance or forensic expert opinion
observations: The first 56 thumbnails show gradual reframing of a skyline, including a large background facade amid cloud and a dark foreground building on the right.

The adjacent source frames 175 and 176 show an abrupt global change in framing and cloud configuration. Native frame 175 also has a narrow strip of inconsistent-looking image content at the bottom edge; this has not received a field/interlace/compression analysis.
The post-change image still includes a broad background facade next to the cloud. The coarse-screen impression must not be promoted to a finding that the whole facade disappeared in this interval.

Frames after the transition show continued cloud development and modest camera movement. No second comparably conspicuous whole-scene replacement was identified in this 90-thumbnail screen. That is not a full continuity audit.
inference: A picture discontinuity is directly visible; an edit or source interruption is strongly indicated, but these images alone do not identify how it arose or its physical-time gap. Do not treat the adjacent-frame spacing as the duration of the underlying physical change.
alternatives_and_limits: An edit, dropped material, camera reframe coupled with an unpreserved interval, or other source-chain processing can account for a discontinuity. A specific editor, original capture continuity, intent or concealment is not identified.
Do not infer building identity, support loss, event time, audio continuity, original microphone association or collapse cause from this screen.
No automated motion measurement, pixel-difference threshold, image enhancement or interpolated frame was used. Native RGB derivatives and thumbnail sheets come from the declared extractor.
Two extraction runs completed. Independent actual-pixel/clock verification remains pending when these observations are frozen.
